Topics · Is there a God?

Does revelation mean switching off my reason?

Reason can find a Maker, but not what the Maker says. How the two work together, what if they seem to clash.

Part 1 of 3

﴿أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌ يَعْقِلُونَ بِهَآ أَوْ ءَاذَانٌ يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا ۖ فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعْمَى ٱلْأَبْصَـٰرُ وَلَـٰكِن تَعْمَى ٱلْقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِى فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

So have they not traveled through the earth and have hearts by which to reason and ears by which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts.

Quran · Al-Hajj 22:46

Translation

‘Hear this now, foolish people without understanding, who have eyes, and don’t see, who have ears, and don’t hear:

Original · Hebrew

שִׁמְעוּ־נָ֣א זֹ֔את עַ֥ם סָכָ֖ל וְאֵ֣ין לֵ֑ב עֵינַ֤יִם לָהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א יִרְא֔וּ אָזְנַ֥יִם לָהֶ֖ם וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁמָֽעוּ׃

Jeremiah · 5:21

World English Bible

﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَمِعُونَ ٱلْقَوْلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحْسَنَهُۥٓ ۚ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ۖ وَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمْ أُو۟لُوا۟ ٱلْأَلْبَـٰبِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones Allāh has guided, and those are people of understanding.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:18

Translation

It came to pass, as he said these things, a certain woman out of the multitude lifted up her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that bore you, and the breasts which nursed you!” But he said, “On the contrary, blessed are those who hear the word of God, and keep it.”

Original · Ancient Greek

Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ λέγειν αὐτὸν ταῦτα ἐπάρασά τις φωνὴν γυνὴ ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακαρία ἡ κοιλία ἡ βαστάσασά σε καὶ μαστοὶ οὓς ἐθήλασας· αὐτὸς δὲ εἶπεν· Μενοῦν μακάριοι οἱ ἀκούοντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ φυλάσσοντες.

the Gospel (Luke) · 11:27-28

World English Bible

The fear is fair. Many people have been told to stop asking. So look at what this text actually asks for. This sentence asks why people do not travel the land and have hearts to reason with or ears to hear with. Two ways of knowing stand side by side: what you work out, and what you are told. You already live by both. No one discovers everything alone, and no one believes a stranger for no reason. The question is not which to drop.

A question for you

What has been your experience of reason and religion?

If you sayI was told not to question.
ThenThat happened to many people, and the lines here ask for the opposite. There is a place to begin again.
If you sayReligion seems to me to be against reason.
ThenThen test it here, and hold this text to what it asks.
If you sayThey have gone together for me.
ThenThen you may be able to say how: what has reason given your faith, and what has faith given your reason?

Part 2 of 3

﴿فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ حَنِيفًا ۚ فِطْرَتَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّتِى فَطَرَ ٱلنَّاسَ عَلَيْهَا ۚ لَا تَبْدِيلَ لِخَلْقِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ ذَٰلِكَ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْقَيِّمُ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

So direct your face [i.e., self] toward the religion, inclining to truth. [Adhere to] the fiṭrah[1145] of Allāh upon which He has created [all] people. No change should there be in the creation of Allāh.[1146] That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.

Translator's notes

[1145] The natural inborn inclination of man to worship his Creator prior to the corruption of his nature by external influences. Thus, Islāmic monotheism is described as the religion of fiṭrah - that of the inherent nature of mankind. [1146] i.e., let people remain true to their fiṭrah within the religion of Islām.

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:30

Translation

(for when Gentiles who don’t have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves, in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them)

Original · Ancient Greek

ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ποιῶσιν, οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος· οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν, συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων,

Romans · 2:14-15

World English Bible

Think of what reason can and cannot reach. It can reason to a Source. It can see that cruelty is wrong. It cannot tell you whether that Source has spoken, how to turn back after a wrong, or what exactly follows death. Those would have to be told, as the name of a stranger's mother has to be told. So the two are not rivals. One opens the question, and the other, if real, answers it. This sentence names sound human nature as where the message lands.

A question for you

Which question do you think reason alone cannot settle?

If you sayWhether there is a God.
ThenSome think so. Several Steps here try to go part of the way, and you can judge them.
If you sayWhat God wants of me.
ThenThat is where most classical thinkers drew the line. The question after it is who tells, and how their truthfulness can be known.
If you sayNone. Reason is enough.
ThenThat is an old position, held by serious thinkers in Islamic history too. Its test is whether it can tell you how to turn back after a wrong, and what follows death.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَإِذَا فَعَلُوا۟ فَـٰحِشَةً قَالُوا۟ وَجَدْنَا عَلَيْهَآ ءَابَآءَنَا وَٱللَّهُ أَمَرَنَا بِهَا ۗ قُلْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْفَحْشَآءِ ۖ أَتَقُولُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when they commit an immorality, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allāh has ordered us to do it." Say, "Indeed, Allāh does not order immorality. Do you say about Allāh that which you do not know?"

Quran · Al-A'raf 7:28

Translation

For the wisdom of the Lord is great. He is mighty in power, and sees all things. His eyes are upon those who fear him. He knows every act of man. He has not commanded any man to be ungodly. He has not given any man license to sin.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ὅτι πολλὴ σοφία τοῦ Κυρίου, ἰσχυρὸς ἐν δυναστείᾳ καὶ βλέπων τὰ πάντα. Καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς φοβουμένους αὐτὸν, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπιγνώσεται πᾶν ἔργον ἀνθρώπου. Καὶ οὐκ ἐνετείλατο οὐδενὶ ἀσεβεῖν, καὶ οὐκ ἔδωκεν ἄνεσιν οὐδενὶ ἁμαρτάνειν.

Sirach · 15:18-20

World English Bible

What if they seem to clash? Ibn Rushd of Cordoba gave a rule: truth does not oppose truth. If a sound proof and a true revelation seem to conflict, one of two things has slipped: the reasoning or the reading. This sentence shows the second slip. People do something shameful and say God commanded it. The reply is that He does not command that. So a claim about what God wants gets no free pass. Who decides when readers and scholars differ? That is still disputed.

A question for you

When a text and your reasoning seem to clash, what do you do first?

If you sayCheck my reasoning again.
ThenThat takes humility, and your reasoning may indeed be at fault.
If you sayCheck how the text has been read.
ThenThat is what many classical scholars did. It asks for more learning than one person has, so you may want help.
If you saySet the text aside.
ThenThen you have settled that case for now. An open question remains: how to judge a whole book from one hard part.
